title: Introduce ghost-surface variant and press-lag visual regression sweep
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Introduce a new button variant called 'ghost-surface' tailored for high-density surfaces and edge cases where buttons visually merge with container backgrounds (list rows, compact chips, table cells). Simultaneously perform a visual regression sweep to address press/hover flicker and the disabled->rehydrate layout jump observed in recent product QA and customer bug reports.

Problem statement: Two related UX regressions were surfaced over the last two cycles: 1) In density/compact contexts icon-only and ghost buttons exhibit a visible border/alpha flicker during pointer transitions (perceived as jitter) because of token blending + conflicting CSS transitions; 2) Buttons that transition from disabled (waiting for async confirmation) back to enabled cause an abrupt visual reflow and a change in baseline (we're calling this 'rehydration') — users reported this as distracting and confusing in form flows. These are most evident in narrow rows and RTL edge-cases.

Goals:
- Define 'ghost-surface' visual spec that: preserves a consistent a11y contrast at rest, removes abrupt stroke/alpha flicker on hover/press, and integrates with semantic tokens so platform teams can opt-in per-surface.
- Introduce a non-blocking hover debounce (design-suggested 60-100ms) and a press smoothing animation that prioritizes transform/opacity over expensive box-shadow repaints.
- Formalize token names and migration notes so engineering can adopt without breaking existing variants.
- Run a full visual regression sweep across components that reuse button tokens (tables, chips, icon lists) and ship a canary rollout with metrics.

Deliverables:
- Figma spec and token table for ghost-surface (hover/press/focus/disabled states).
- Component change RFC describing new prop: variant="ghost-surface" and new prop: hoverDebounceMs.
- Token migration guide mapping legacy ghost tokens -> ghost-surface tokens and fallback behavior.
- QA checklist, visual diff suite, and Storybook stories demonstrating dense/normal/RTL modes.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Debounce latency: longer debounces remove flicker but can create perceived sluggishness for keyboard users. To avoid this we scope debounce to pointer events only and preserve immediate keyboard focus state (no debounce).
- Animation approach: using transforms/opacities avoids layout repaints but requires some color blending emulation for stroke thinning; we tested two approaches in prototype and chose a 3-layer approach (base background overlay, icon/label layer, 1px surface stroke implemented as composited outline) to keep paint costs low.

Open questions for Eng:
- Can the runtime component accept hoverDebounceMs as a top-level prop in our React primitives without breaking server-side rendering hydration? (ENG-50212)
- Perf measurement plan: what thresholds for jank increase are acceptable for canary (P95 frame time + layout thrash count)?

References & artifacts: see links field for Figma, Confluence, and prototypes.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec uploaded: Figma file includes ghost-surface states for normal/compact/RTL and token table
Token names added to semantic token registry and migration guide created
Component stories: ghost-surface displayed in Storybook with pointer/keyboard interaction demos
Hover debounce implemented for pointer events only; keyboard focus remains immediate
Visual diff run shows no new regressions in tables, chips, and icon lists (baseline approved)
Canary rollout plan documented and smoke metrics defined (P95 latency, visual-jank count)
Accessibility: focus ring visible, contrast ratio >= 3:1 for icon-only ghost-surface at small sizes, keyboard nav tests green
